item.title: Covering a volunteer shift
item.description: Arrange for someone to cover a shift and help run the activity desk at a public event.

children.definition: To put your name on a list to show that you want to do something.
children.example: You can sign up for the morning shift at the activity desk when the list goes online on Monday.

children.definition: To do someone else's duties for a short time when they cannot do them.
children.example: Could you fill in for me at the activity desk from two to four while I'm at the dentist?
collocations: fill in for someone at short notice

children.definition: To arrive at a place or event.
children.example: Please turn up ten minutes before your shift so I can show you where we keep the activity leaflets.

children.definition: A list that shows who is supposed to work at different times.
children.example: The duty roster shows that Nargiza is at the activity desk until noon and Pavel is there after lunch.

children.definition: A piece of paper where people write their names to show that they have come.
children.example: Put your name on the sign-in sheet when you get to the activity desk so the organiser knows you're here.
collocations: leave the sign-in sheet at the desk

children.definition: To gather things together and put them away or into bags or boxes, usually when you have finished an activity.
children.example: After the last visitors leave, please pack up the unused activity sheets and put the box under the desk.
children.translation_uz: narsalarni yigʻishtirib, quti yoki xaltaga joylamoq
collocations: pack up at the end of the day

children.definition: To arrange things on a surface so people can see or use them easily.
children.example: Before the doors open, lay out the activity leaflets across the front of the desk so visitors can see their choices.
collocations: lay out the materials on a table

children.definition: To give a copy or one of several things to each person in a group.
children.example: Could you give out a programme to each person who comes to the activity desk?

children.definition: A small sign you wear that tells people who you are or what your role is.
children.example: Clip your badge to your jacket so visitors can see your name and know to ask you for help.

children.definition: Ready to come and work if someone contacts you and asks for help.
children.example: I'm on call until three, so ring me if the afternoon volunteer can't come.
children.translation_ru: на связи и готов выйти по вызову
children.translation_uz: aloqada va chaqirishsa ishga chiqishga tayyor
collocations: stay on call until closing time

children.definition: A period of time set aside or available for an activity.
children.example: The only time slot still free at the activity desk is from four to five.

children.definition: To have none of something left.
children.example: If you run out of programmes at the activity desk, there are more in the cupboard.
children.translation_ru: остаться без чего-либо; исчерпать запас чего-либо

children.definition: To look at or talk through information carefully so it is clear.
children.example: Can we go over the instructions for the activity desk before you leave?

children.definition: Before something happens or before the time when something is needed.
children.example: If you can't work your Sunday shift, tell the organiser in advance so there's time to find someone else.
